In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no theoretical evidence that a light Higgs bosons mass of about 120 GeV is impossible to obtain within the Minimal Supersymmetry Model.
the lightest Higgs boson is expected to have a mass around 125 GeV in a large region of the MSSM parameter space, and this mass is stable under radiative corrections.
the Higgs mass is enhanced by the stop sector, and the size of the enhancement is determined by the stop masses and mixing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of a hierarchical stop spectrum, the light Higgs mass is enhanced by the QCD and Yukawa couplings at two-loop leading-logarithmic level, but is reduced at two-loop next-to-leading-logarithmic level.
in the limit of large top-Yukawa coupling, and large stop mass hierarchy, the light Higgs mass is driven by a logarithmic running from M t 1 to M t 2, and then to the top mass.
, for the light Higgs mass, the two-loop leading and non-leading logarithmic corrections to be included are those coming from top-Yukawa and QCD couplings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-loop leading and non-leading logarithmic corrections to the light Higgs mass are not negligible in the presence of a large stop hierarchy.
, for the case of a hierarchical stop spectrum, the leading logarithmic corrections to the Higg boson mass are not necessarily dominated by the top-Yukawa coupling.
the lightest Higgs boson is expected to be lighter than 120 GeV for stop masses of order the top quark mass, even in the case of a large stop mass hierarchy.
